h1. The general guidelines for the deep-dives

Deep-dives \[into rider tickets submitted through the FAQ articles] are aimed to give a deeper understanding of the users' needs, questions, and struggles. These insights are planned to be used as a basis for hypotheses about needed content and for future revamped FAQ articles.

* How to understand whether an article needs deep-dive?
* How to choose tickets for a deep-dive?
* How to review tickets (deep-dive instructions)?
* How to analyse deep-dive results?
* How to analyse all found data?
* How to present found data and deep-dive results?
* How to follow up deep-dive and article changes?


h3. How to understand whether an article needs deep-dive?

Preparation steps:

* Map out the potential content of an article and decide its purpose
** Self-help instruction *or* description of the problem and instruction on how to contact us (i.e. self-help guidelines *or* entry point for a ticket)
* Analyse available data on self-help deflection, number of incoming tickets, ATIs breakdown for incoming tickets, and avg number of replies per ticket

Deep-dives into rider tickets are needed in the following situations:

* An article contains self-help instructions (no CS help should be needed) but there are still incoming tickets with a relevant ATI
* An article is an entry point (CS help is needed) and
** The avg number of replies per ticket is high
** The analysis of ATIs of incoming tickets does not provide any useful information

In other cases, Looker data analysis and, if needed, small deep-dive (review of incoming tickets marked with relevant or irrelevant ATIs) is enough.

*NB\!* Looker data analysis is a crucial and necessary part of each article review and revamp.

h3. How to choose tickets for a deep-dive?

Criteria to choose tickets for a deep-dive:

* Incoming tickets submitted through an article via in-app marked with relevant ATI(s), i.e. ATIs corresponding to an article’s topic
** Tickets submitted for a particular quarter (e.g. Q2 or Q3)
* Randomly chosen 250-300 tickets (125-150 tickets per agent if there are 2 agents; 100 tickets per agent if there are 3 agents)

*NB\!* Looking into all incoming tickets may provide more insights into global issues but might take more time because of the translation issues.

To fin all incoming tickets submitted through an article, use filter _Self Help Article Entry Point_ in Looker.

h3. How to review tickets (deep-dive instructions)?

If *an article contains self-help instructions*, the questions for deep-dive:

* Information requested is in the article – _Yes/No_
* The user could (potentially) solve the issue themselves – _Yes/No_
* The question topic – _Exact sum, Country-specific info, Clear self-help instruction, CS help needed - self-help does not work_ (if chosen, a reason is required: _No self-help option, App issue, Other_)_, Wrong info in the article, Other_ (if _Other_, the comment is needed)
* General observations, comments

If *an article is an entry point*, the questions for deep-dive:

* An explanation of the issue is in the article – _Yes/No_
* The user could (potentially) solve the issue themselves – _Yes/No_
* The user provided all the needed details to solve the issue – _Yes/No_ (if avg number of replies per ticket is high)
* The issue reason – _Rider action, Driver action, System action, No issue,_ _Other_ (if _Other_, the comment is needed)
** Might be different based on the initial question to be checked or answered
* General observations, comments

h3. How to analyse deep-dive results?

Deep-dive results can be divided into 4 categories based on the outcome and possible actions:

||Information requested is in the article
*or*
An explanation of the issue is in the article||The user could (potentially) solve the issue themselves||The question topic
*or*
The issue reason|| ||
|Yes|Yes|Filter by the reason or topic chosen|Ideas on how improve the wording/text (self-help instructions)|
|Yes|No|Filter by the reason or topic chosen|Ideas on how to improve the wording/text of the current article (instructions on how to contact support)
Ideas for future automations|
|No|Yes|Filter by the reason or topic chosen|Ideas what self-help instructions are missing and might be added|
|No|No|Filter by the reason or topic chosen|Ideas on what instructions when and how to contact support are missing
Ideas for future automations|

h3. How to analyse all found data?

The possible ways to analyse all the results and found data:

* Review the ATIs of the incoming tickets
** How many tickets are related to the article topic?
** What are the other ATIs? Do we have or plan to have any articles for other ATIs?
** Are other ATIs related to the article topic? If not, what could be the reasons for users using this article to contact CS? Are other ATIs related to the article title?
*** A small review of incoming tickets marked with irrelevant ATIs is possible (10-50 tickets to see the patterns or possible reasons)
* Review the market division of the incoming tickets
** In which countries do users contact us more often on the topic? What can be an issue in those countries?
*** A small additional review of incoming tickets in these markets is possible (10-50 tickets to see the patterns or possible reasons)
* Review the average replies per article
** What is the average number? Is the average number high?
** Is there a way to reduce the number of replies per ticket? For example, writing down what information to provide when contacting the support team.
* Review the deep-dive results 
** How many tickets were related to the questions about exact sum/country-specific info?
** How is the current self-help instruction or instruction on how to contact CS clear?
** How many tickets could have been solved the user themselves? What are the reasons why are the user can’t solve the issue themselves?
** Do we need localised articles with the country-specific information?

h3. How to present found data and deep-dive results?

The format to present deep-dive results and article changes:

* % of the incoming tickets that might be deflected if an article has or does not have some specific information. Thus, an article was changed \[description of a change] or not \[reason behind a decision].
* % of the incoming tickets that might be solved faster if an article contains some specific information or instructions on how to contact the support team. Thus, an article was changed \[description of a change] or not \[reason behind a decision].
* % of incoming tickets with ATIs irrelevant to an article topic were submitted through an article because an article has or does not have some specific information. Thus, an article was changed \[description of a change] or not \[reason behind a decision].
* % of incoming tickets were sent by users in certain markets because an article has or does not have some specific information. Thus, a localised version of an article was changed \[description of a change] or not \[reason behind a decision].

h3. How to follow up deep-dive and article changes? TBC

After a deep-dive and/or Looker data analysis is performed and an article is changed, possible ways to follow up and review results:

* Monitor self-help deflection and number of incoming tickets on a weekly basis during a first month after changes were actioned; on a monthly basis afterwards
* In case of some drastic or unexpected changes, a small deep-dive into incoming tickets can be organised after a month after changes were actioned
* afr, ren-cen, ren-glob, na, au is not yet checked

{code:sql}with avg_deploy as (
select name, external_id, avg(diff) avg_deploy_in_sec, count(*) number_of_deployments 
from 
(select de.id,
		de.created,
		de.lat,
		de.lng,
		external_id,
		c.name,
		LAG(de.created) OVER (partition by external_id order by de.created asc) prev_created,
		date_diff('second',LAG(de.created) OVER (partition by external_id order by de.created asc),de.created) diff
from 
rental.rental_order_charger_action_deploy_event de
join rental.rental_order_charger_action_deploy d
on de.charger_action_deploy_id=d.id and de.connection_id=d.connection_id
join rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc on d.search_category_id=sc.id
join admin_system_city c on sc.city_id=c.id
where de.created>date'2020-08-01' and de.to_state = 'deployed' 
order by d.external_id asc, de.created asc
)
where diff<3600
group by 1,2),
avg_collect as (
select name, external_id, avg(diff) avg_collect_in_sec, count(*) number_of_collections
from 
(select 
	ce.id,
	ce.created,
	ce.lat,
	ce.lng,
	cl.external_id,
	c.name,
	LAG(ce.created) OVER (partition by external_id order by ce.created asc) prev_created,
	date_diff('second',LAG(ce.created) OVER (partition by external_id order by ce.created asc),ce.created) diff
from rental.rental_order_charger_action_collect_event ce
join rental.rental_order_charger_action_collect cl
on ce.charger_action_collect_id=cl.id and ce.connection_id=cl.connection_id
join rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc 
	on cl.search_category_id=sc.id
join admin_system_city c 
	on sc.city_id=c.id
where ce.created>date'2020-08-01' 
	and ce.to_state = 'collected' 
	and ce.from_state is null 
order by cl.external_id asc, ce.created asc
)
where diff<3600
group by 1,2
)
select d.name,
	d.external_id,
	avg_deploy_in_sec,
	number_of_deployments,
	avg_collect_in_sec,
	number_of_collections
from avg_deploy d
join avg_collect c on d.name=c.name and d.external_id=c.external_id
order by name asc, external_id asc

Discussed with Andre Ilie, replacing the training job with a tuning job using Bayesian search is simplest way to meet his needs.  We also need a way for winning HPs from tuning to be dumped to S3, and for training jobs to be able to read HPs from S3 (at execute-time) instead of having them hardcoded in the config.  Probably a long-lived XCom could be useful here.

Since Andre initially wanted multiple sequential tuning jobs per group-branch, for tuning different parameters independently of each other (to shrink search space), I  consider a more composable way to specify Airpipe stages with custom ordering and structure e.g.

{noformat}steps: [
  { type: 'query', config: { ... } },
  { type: 'map', config: { ... } },
  { type: 'tune', config: { ... } },
  { type: 'train', config: { ... } },
  { type: 'train', config: { ... } },
  { type: 'reduce', config: { ... } },
  { type: 'deploy', config: { ... } },
]{noformat}

We’d need some convention for how XComs are used to pass output path from one stage to input of next stage.

We’d also need a way to specify “map” and “reduce” (fork/join) operations for making branches (potentially nested\!), and allowing them to converge again at some later point.

Interesting.  Current Airpipe could then be used as a highly-opinionated generator for one of these more versatile configs, which another generator then parses to build stages and plump them via XComs.

from 
(select de.id,

		de.lat,

		c.name,

		LAG(de.lng) OVER (partition by external_id order by de.created asc) prev_lng,

rental.rental_order_charger_action_deploy_event de
join rental.rental_order_charger_action_deploy d

join rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc on d.search_category_id=sc.id

avg_collect as (
select 
	name, 
	external_id, 
	avg(diff) avg_collect_in_sec, 
	count(*) number_of_collections,
	1.0*count(case when dist<10 then id else null end)/NULLIF((number_of_collections-count(case when dist<10 then id else null end)),0)+1 batch_size
from 
(select 
	ce.id,
	ce.created,
	ce.lat,
	ce.lng,
	cl.external_id,
	c.name,
	LAG(ce.created) OVER (partition by external_id order by ce.created asc) prev_created,
	LAG(ce.lat) OVER (partition by external_id order by ce.created asc) prev_lat,
	LAG(ce.lng) OVER (partition by external_id order by ce.created asc) prev_lng,
	ST_DistanceSphere(ST_Point(ce.lng, ce.lat),ST_Point(prev_lng, prev_lat)) as dist,
	date_diff('second',LAG(ce.created) OVER (partition by external_id order by ce.created asc),ce.created) diff

join rental.rental_order_charger_action_collect cl

Please be aware that non-competition obligation is still valid during your employment contract with Bolt Technology OÜ and does not concern confidentiality obligation you have towards Bolt Technology OÜ._* 

Having the non-competition obligation in your agreements after termination does not serve the initial purpose anymore as the company has grown. -As it’s really hard to prove whether the non-competition clause after the termination of the employment contract has been followed or not, we have decided to remove this clause from the future contracts and withdraw it from the existing employment contracts.- Furthermore, Bolt doesn’t want to limit your further job opportunities.

Should you have any additional questions or concerns regarding the withdrawal of the non-competition obligation, feel free to contact your manager or your People Partner for more information.


Small FAQ

*What is non-competition obligation?*
A non-compete obligation is a contract between an employee and an employer in which the employee agrees not to enter into competition with the employer during or after employment. This clause is included in your employment contract.

*Does it mean now, that I can work also for a competitor during the employment contract and after my employment contract will be terminated?*
The NCA will be still in place during your employment in Bolt, meaning that you cannot work for competitor now, but after the employment contract will be terminated, Bolt does not restrict you to choose whichever employer you would like (also not competitor).

*Does it mean I cannot be Wolt courier during my employment?*
No, you can work as a Wolt courier, but why not to be Bolt courier?

{code:sql}with flags_and_targets as 
(
select id, created,vehicle_id,type, from_state, to_state, value as mask, charge, lat, lng
from rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event
where created between date'2020-06-01' and date'2020-08-15' 
and (type='marker_mask' or (from_state = 'operational' and to_state='collected'))
and connection_id='company_tallinn'
order by vehicle_id asc, created asc
)
select *,
	(prev_mask>>0)%2 AS flag_1_USER_BAD_FEEDBACK,
	(prev_mask>>1)%2 AS flag_2_SYSTEM_SUSPICIOUS_RIDE, 
	(prev_mask>>2)%2 AS flag_3_USER_CANCELLED, 
	(prev_mask>>3)%2 AS flag_4_USER_REPORTED, 
	(prev_mask>>4)%2 AS flag_5_CHARGER_REPORTED, 
	(prev_mask>>5)%2 AS flag_6_ADMIN_REPORTED_PROBLEM, 
	(prev_mask>>6)%2 AS flag_7_SYSTEM_TOO_MANY_ERRORS_RECEIVED, 
	(prev_mask>>7)%2 AS flag_8_VEHICLE_ON_ACTIVE_SHIFT,
	(prev_mask>>8)%2 AS flag_9_VEHICLE_ON_SCHEDULED_SHIFT,	
	(prev_mask>>9)%2 AS flag_10_USER_TOO_MANY_BAD_FEEDBACKS_RECEIVED,	
	(prev_mask>>10)%2 AS flag_11_VEHICLE_REPORTED,	
	(prev_mask>>11)%2 AS flag_12_VEHICLE_SWAPPING_BATTERY,
	(prev_mask>>12)%2 AS flag_13_VEHICLE_MISSING,
	(prev_mask>>13)%2 AS flag_14_VEHICLE_HARD_TO_REACH,
	(prev_mask>>14)%2 AS flag_15_VEHICLE_NOT_HIDE_FROM_ORDER_ON_ACTIVE_SHIFT,
	(prev_mask>>15)%2 AS flag_16_NEW_FLAG_2,
	(prev_mask>>16)%2 AS flag_17_NEW_FLAG_3
from
( 
select *,
lag(mask,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by id asc) as prev_mask
from flags_and_targets
order by vehicle_id desc, id asc
)
where to_state='collected' 
order by vehicle_id desc, id asc{code}

Dear Anna,

In order to avoid "accusation of making misleading claims", we have to be internally certain that every numeric/% claim, especially when that puts our platform product/offer above someone else's product/offer (traditional taxi), can be backed up by some credible & verifiable study, search and/or data sources. 

Thus such claims cannot be made just on the basis of gut feeling or general perception that Bolt is usually cheaper. 

In markets with stricter advertising controls (such as UK) it is expected that your clarify this _(what sources, studies or methods have been used to arrive at values of the claim)_ in the very same text of the add (small-text footnote or similar). 

Thus I am not sure at all that "compared to regular taxis" is good enough - at least for the UK and markets with similarly high expectations . 

Great new is that this is not new topic to the marketing team. If possible, please consult within the team - e.g. with Liam Wentworth from UK _(he worked recently on London Underground campaign and had to find solution for similar claims & challenges)_.

If you have any additional legal questions - please call me +3725065670 it is more efficient if we cover other outstanding questions (if any) via call.

Kind regards,

Ahto

it’s really good to know about our privacy policy and testing, as some feature tests raise a lot of concerns from the operation side.

Regarding the feature we want to continue testing:

We will show a matched driver before the driver confirms. This way a rider doesn’t have to wait for too long to see that we got the order and they will be picked up. Atm. a rider sees a spinning animation with a message that we are looking for a driver until we get confirmation, that sometimes takes more than 20 sec. and results in cancellations, as the user might think we can’t find a driver or the app is broken.

In ca. 70% of the cases the driver we showed is the driver who will arrive at a pick up point. In case the driver we displayed rejects, we will search for a new one and display updated information, so the rider will see the update. This is not an entirely new behaviour, exactly the same happens in case a driver first accepts an order and then rejects it.

Hope that helps to clarify our intentions.

Approach to measure how passes decrease churn:

# We take all users, that had their first ride at least 30 rides prior to launching passes in a specific city
# We divide them by their riding pattern before pass launch
# We divide them by their riding pattern after pass launch
# We divide them by their riding pattern after their last subscription expired if we have at least 2 weeks of history (that means that we take only users with last pass expired before Sep 11)
# We define usage transition types for two cases (2)->(3) and (2)->(4)

Transition types

* increased - changed their riding pattern in the direction of higher activity
* decreased - changed their riding pattern in the direction of lower activity
* no change or unclear - did not change riding pattern, or one of the patterns was ‘not clear'

h3. Incoming tickets with the ATI Driver Took a Longer Route by FAQ entry point – General conclusions

* ~54.8% of the incoming tickets were received through the article on _Price Higher Than Expected_
* ~29.4% of the incoming tickets were received through the article on _Driver Took a Longer Route_
* 3.65% of the incoming tickets were sent via the articles in driver behaviour (_Driver was Rude, Reporting an Accident_)
* 4% of the incoming tickets were sent via the article on changes to price (_Price Estimation, Unauthorised Charges_, etc.)

=> Most of the users may submit the overcharged complaints without choosing a specific reason for the overcharge.

h3. Deep-dive into received tickets through the article - General observations

Randomly chosen 45 tickets received in June-August and marked by ATI _Driver Took a Longer Route_ were [reviewed|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gCIwt0mGuOm0MQ-LzElK0zsifTQbaRedat0mq7q4TgM/edit?usp=sharing].

* Reports about the ride in the UK were also related to not understanding the estimate price (the minimum-maximum sum). The users did not pay attention to the sum before ordering a ride.
* Almost all the reports were related to the overcharge (almost no report about the route without stating that the price is higher).

Note: No % or numbers are mentioned here as the number of the tickets reviewed is low.

h1. Insights and proposals

*FAQ on Driver Took a Pour Route:*

* No additional information is required from the users when they contact support. Nevertheless, a short description of their issue would be always useful.
* An explanation that the system proposes the most effective route but a driver can take a different one and a route choice can be discussed before the trip/mid-trip.
* Link to the article on Price Higher than Expected might be useful (see the reason below). Longer route reports are almost all connected to the overcharge reports; not so many reports of the bad route without complaint about being overcharged.
* No country-specific information is required.

*FAQ in general:*

* The general information on why the price can differ might be useful (e.g. toll fees, wait time fees, additional stops, changing the destination). As users report price higher than expected through the article on a longer route, it might mean that they lack knowledge of what else can go wrong.
* Instructions on how to check the price components (invoice received) might be added as well.
* Clear instructions for the UK market on estimate price (minimum/maximum but depends on the route and traffic) might be useful.

Vaatasin üüripindade asendamise kokkuleppe üle ja mul on selle kohta järgmised kommentaarid:

*Põhjenduspunkt B*: Nimetatud punkti järgi on _Pooled on kokku leppinud, et teevad koostööd selleks, et leida Ruumidele maksejõulised asendusüürnikud mitte halvematel tingimustel, kui on need, mis on toodud Lepingus._ Selle lause peaks kokkleppest välja võtma või ümber sõnastama selliselt, et poolte ühiseks eesmärgiks ei ole mitte üksnes sellise asendusüürniku lepidmine, kes sõlmiks üürileandjaga lepingu samadel või parematel tingimustel kui on tänane leping Boltiga, vaid ükskõik millise asendusüürniku leidmine. Loogika siis selles, et kui üürileandja leiab asendusüürniku, kes on nõus maksma väiksemat üüri kui Bolt, siis on Boltil võimalik hüvitada üürileandjale kahe üüri vahe ja selle tõttu ei tohiks üürileandjal olla õigust keelduda sellise asendusüürniku aktsepteerimisest. Tänane sõnastus võib meile halvast kätte maksta juhul, kui üürileandja ei leia pikema aja jooksul uut üürniku ja me soovime üürilepingu ise erakorraliselt üles öelda ja oleme nõus hüvitama kulud, mis võrduvad üüriga tähtaja lõpuni miinus asendusüürniku üür (nii hoiaksime kokku kommunaalide kulud). Üürileandja poolt väljapakutud sõnastus paneks meid sellisel juhul halvemasse olukorda, kui me oleks tänase kohtupraktika järgi.

*Tagatisraha*: Praeguse lahenduse järgi vähendame üüripinda selliselt, et igakuiseks üüriks on ca 11 tuhat eurot, kuid tagatisraha meile tagasi ei anta, vaid see jääb tagama üürileandja võimalikke tulevasi nõudeid. Selline lahendus ei ole kindlasit loogiline ja ei peaks olema meie poolt aktsepteeritav. Lepingu järgi peaks tagatisraha olema 2 kuu üüri suurune, kuid praegu pakutakse meile lahendust, kus tagatisraha on ca 4 kuu üüri suurune (skeem sisuliselt selline, et pidasid vähendame, kuid vähendatavate pindade tagatisraha kohe tagasi ei anta, vaid need jäävad tagama meie muid kohustusi).

*Tagastatavate pindade seisukord*: Kokkuleppe järgi tuleb pinnad anda tagasi üürilepingu 11 peatükis kirjeldatud seisukorras, mis võib sõltuvalt pindade tegelikust seisukorrast tuua Boltile kaasa täiendavate kulustuste tegemise kohustuse. Ma saan aru, et tegelik olukord on see, et uus üürnik tahab kasutada meie sisekujundust, sh Bolti poolt maha pandud vaipasid jne. Selles valguses peaks leping väljendama seda, et anname pinnad üürileandjale tagasi sellises seisus nagu need on täna (v.a et viime ära üüripinnal olevad Bolti asjad). Üürileandjal on võimalik uue üürnikuga sõlmitavas lepingus reguleerida seda, et need pinnad lähevad uuele üürnikule üle samuti nii nagu need täna on.

Lepingus tuleks täiendaalt reguleerida ka seda, millise tähtaja jooksul saab üürileandja tugineda puudustele, mis avastatakse pärast üüripinna uuele üürnikule üleandmist. Seaduse järgi on üürileandjal võimalik sellistele puudustele tugineda 6 kuud, kuid arvestades seda, et pinnad hõivatakse kohe uue üürniku pool ja hiljem ei ole eristatav, kes on puuduse tekitanud, oleks mõistlik limiteerida puudustele tuginemise tähtaega lühema ajaga, näiteks 1 kuuga. Üürileandjal on võimalik uue üürnikuga sõlmitavas lepingus reguleerida, et uus üürnik kohustusb puudustest teavitama 1 kuu jooksul.

*Asenduspindade seisukord*: Kuna vahetame osad senised pinnad uute pindade vastu, tuleks lepingu kajastata ka seda, millise seisukorras antakse üle uued pinnad ja millises seisukorras me need üürileandjale tagastame. Juhul, kui me asenduspindasid ise kasutusse ei võta ja need seisavad tühjana, tuleks igaks juhuks lepingusse selgelt kirja panna ka see, et me ei vastuta ühegi üüripinna puuduse eest ja tagastame selle seisukorras, nagu me selle enda kätte saime.

*Pind nr 16 tagastamine*: Jääb mõnevõrra arusaamatuks, miks on vaja käesoleva lepinguga reguleerida ka selle pinna tagastamist. )
SELECT
sc.country_code as country,
o.id as order_id,
o.created,
listagg(bi.payment_method_type,',') as payment_method_type,
o.master_user_id as user_id,
DATEDIFF('day',u.created,o.created) as user_age,
CASE WHEN '+'||uu.phone<>sco.phone_prefix THEN 1 ELSE 0 END as foreign_phone,

(CASE WHEN c.target='item_price' THEN c.price_after_discount/r.rate+o.delivery_price/r.rate ELSE o.total_price/r.rate END) as price_eur,

LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_courier AS oc ON oc.order_provider_id = op.id AND oc.state = 'delivered'
LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_order_payment_info as pi ON pi.connection_id=o.connection_id AND pi.order_id=o.id

      CASE WHEN POSITION('card' IN listagg(payment_method_type,','))>0 THEN 'card' WHEN POSITION('cash' IN listagg(payment_method_type,','))>0 THEN 'cash' ELSE 'bolt_credit' END  as payment_method_type,

      current_balance as (

      LEFT JOIN payout.invoicing_balance_balance_entry as be ON a.id = be.account_id
      LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates as r ON DATE(r.valid_on)=CURRENT_DATE AND r.currency=a.currency
      WHERE a.type='user_bolt_credit'
      AND be.is_active=TRUE
      GROUP BY 1
      ),
      refunds AS (

      WHERE "type"='refund'
      AND (from_agent_type='global_user'

      CASE WHEN payment_method_group='cash' AND ROUND(COALESCE(bi.booked_amount/r.rate,0),2)<0 THEN 0 ELSE ROUND(COALESCE(bi.booked_amount/r.rate,0),2) END AS balance_credit_eur,

      CASE WHEN payment_method_group='cash' THEN (price_eur-balance_credit_eur-received_cash_from_user_eur-total_refund_eur) ELSE 0 END AS debt_eur,

*Section 10, Indemnification*

This is our standard agreement and when drafting it, it has been carefully worded and balanced to give us the level of protection we and you as a customer need, while at the same time make sure that you as a customer feel comfortable with the agreement. The nature of our service is for us to deliver SMSs fast, secure and safe. For most of our services, you “pay-as-you-go”, meaning that there are no fixed fees for using our platform and you can stop using the service as you wish. Our service does not (and should not) cover any reviewing of the SMSs being sent and make sure that that they are in compliance with local regulations and laws – we act as a post office, we ensure that the mail is delivered and arrives to the address stated on the envelope, we don’t open the mail to review that it has the correct content or that the right person is stated on the envelope. This is the background for why Section 10(b) has been drafted as it is. It is not possible for Sinch to be liable for how you as a customer is using our service, with your data/content. As an example, if you accidently send SPAM messages in a jurisdiction when using our service, a mobile operator can impose fines on Sinch as Sinch is the mobile operator’s contracting party. As we have no control over how/to whom you sent the messages using our platform, we must have acceptable level protection in relation hereto. 

 

Sections 10(a) an 10(b) have been drafted to reflect the relevant risks of each party, and the risks are different. Therefore, it is not possible to copy text from one section and put it in the other section – the wording of the sections would then not be logical. For example, Sinch cannot be liable for “c) Claims arising from or relating to use of the Services (whether +by the Customer or any Service User+)”, that would mean that +Sinch+ liable for the +Customer’s use+ of the service, which is incorrect.

Hi Sandra\!

The most standard action would be to terminate. You can do this quite easily with notice of 30 days(2.3).  With the information you have given, I would not recommend that you terminate immediately (2.4) as I do not feel this consitutes a “material” breach of the agreement. Material generally implies that the breach is in direct contradiction to a stated clause and has had a large impact. As there is no direct prohibition of this use, I think arguing material breach would be challenging. However, you can choose to suspend (2.1) and then terminate but you will need to pay them the agreed fees for suspension (4.1.3).

In addition to terminating, claiming Loss (9.2) for this use is also a possibility as it was unauthorized action by their employees. However, it should be considered if the value of the loss is really worth the hassle and possible dispute. How much has this amounted to? You *must* also be able to evidence and prove that this was being done by *them* and without our consent. If we have any outstanding payment remaining to them then you could offset these (4.5) up to the point needed to cover the losses. Anything not covered by outstanding payment you could claim back from them by having accounting makes you an invoice for scooter rides totalling the amount outstanding. This is because the personal use of our platform was not included in the fees (5.1) and was not an approved expense (5.2).

If you will not terminate and continue to work with them then it would be best you try to resolve this with them more informally and cordially.

Hi\!

I maybe translate here most important takeaways from the Estonian DPA guidance 

* e-mail addresses that refer to a general contact of a business ([info@business.ee|mailto:info@business.ee], [business@business.ee|mailto:business@business.ee]) are business e-mail addresses and they dont require consent.
* e-mail addresses that directly or indirectly refer to a person ([silja.hundt@bolt.eu|mailto:silja.hundt@bolt.eu], [dpo@bolt.eu|mailto:dpo@bolt.eu]) one must consider the position of the person in that business and the character of the service to be marketed. so for example since I am DPO (data protection officer) at bolt, then businesses may send to me directly privacy related marketing messages but not messages about theatre performances for example. which means basically that by sending marketing messages to a business e-mail containing a name or position, then the message must be suitable for that position. so marketing messages related to taxi services sent to taxi drivers should be ok.
* if a person’s e-mail address is marked as the business’s e-mail address in the public business registry, then this e-mail address is considered to be business e-mail address.

So since these individual drivers are also entities, then I suggest that is the Norwegian approach does not differ much, then you may send taxi services related messages to them. The domain does not make any impact. I also add, that regulation foresees the possibility to still unsubscribe for businesses but I understand it is a one-time sending so it will be OK.

Hi Aleksei,

Thank you for your input. Based on the information provided by you, I would strongly recommend to remove the ad in question as it will be very difficult for us to argue that the generic statement of the ad “take Bolt and pay 50% less” is always correct and this is something that we have an obligation to prove under the comparative and misleading advertising rules of Estonian Advertising Act. If we fail to prove, the supervisory authority (Estonian Consumer Protection Board) has an authority to request us to remove the ad anyway and impose a penalty up to the amount of 9600 EUR. In addition to receiving the fine, we risk bad publicity as it is likely that a journalist (Aivar Pau) would pick up the news and publish a negative article that would show Bolt in negative light trying to deceive consumers. Considering that an article has already been published, it is very likely that an additional article will follow: [https://forte.delfi.ee/news/auto/amet-alustas-bolti-suhtes-menetlust?id=91225559|https://forte.delfi.ee/news/auto/amet-alustas-bolti-suhtes-menetlust?id=91225559]

A quick recap of why I deem the ad problematic (despite of the fact that I do sympathise that taking into account the 3EUR discount, a Bolt ride might end up being 50% or more cheaper in most cases:

(1) The identifiable competitors referred to in the ad are ANY TAXIS, meaning that we would have to prove extensively that all of our competitors in Tallinn are 50% or more expensive (not just Tulika, Tallink, Bongo, Yes). The authority might not be satisfied with us referring only to the 4 competitors used in the comparative data provided by you.

(2) The authority is very likely to claim that the statement in the ad “If you need a taxi, don't take a taxi. Take Bolt and pay 50% less.” is a generic statement claiming that a Bolt ride will always be 50% cheaper, even if the discount code is not applied or if not Bolt Basic but other categories of such as Protect, Electric, Premium, XL etc are used. The aim of the Advertising Act here is to ensure that the advertisers do not mislead the consumers and the authority is likely to claim that we have misled the consumers as the ride will not be cheaper if the discount code will not be applied or a different category other than Bolt Basic is used by the consumer. 

(3) We can’t use the data provided by you because (a) it compares the taxi ride prices only against Bolt Basic category only; (b) it gives an example of an “typical” ride in Tallinn without identifying the distance or duration - in order to provide comprehensive comparable data we should provide at least comparative data for the shortest, average and longest possible ride in Tallinn identifying clearly distance; (c) it identifies that the KM PRICE an HOUR PRICE of Bolt Basic is less than 50% cheaper than BongoTakso’s or YesTakso’s; (d) it identified that the “typical ride in Tallinn” is only 32.25% cheaper than BongoTakso and 39.56% cheaper than YesTakso.

*To summarise, it would ONLY make sense for us to pursue our claim that the statement in the ad is correct and not in breach of advertising laws if you are able to provide me with comprehensive evidence that the rides of ALL BOLT CATEGORIES are 50% or more cheaper than the rides with taxis (all bigger Taxi companies in Tallinn, not just the 4 competitors included in the earlier comparison), providing clear comparable data for comparable rides in Tallinn (minimum distance, average distance and maximum possible distance) - ideally WITHOUT TAKING INTO ACCOUNT THE 3 EUR DISCOUNT as the text of the ad is not clear about the fact that Bolt is only cheaper if the discount is applied. And if we decide to pursue the claim, commercial acceptance of the up to 9600 eur fine and potential bad publicity is required as well.* 

As a general takeaway for our marketing team, it would be good to highlight that ads should not mislead, the statements made should be clear and we should have objective proof to support our claims. Thus the current ad should have referred to Bolt Basic category only, identified not all taxis but the competitors who are clearly 50% or more expensive than us, clarified that the price will be cheaper if the discount code is used, identify that this statement applies to rides that are not longer than X KM (not a generic statement that leaves room for the consumer to believe that it applies to any rides, incl rides from one end of Tallinn to the other or even beyond that…).

*Our response deadline is 12.10, therefore, in order to have sufficient time to prepare a response to the authority, I need your response on how you would like to proceed by Tuesday, 6 October the latest. If you decide to take down the ad, I will have to notify the authority that the ad has been removed, which means I need information on when the ad(s) will be removed. If your decision is to proceed with the claim that the statement of the ad is not misleading comparative advertising, I need you to provide me with the proof mentioned above and a confirmation that we’re willing to risk receiving the fine.*

But this is a case how we can shift users from ride-hailing to scooters just by having both of them in one app. People are not only using ride-hailing, but also personal cars. Let’s look at a wider perspective.

‘Micromobility and active travel in the UK' research highlights that 36% of scooter rides worldwide are done instead of car rides. This value is lower in European cities, with 10-20% on average, as they are already seen a significant shift from private cars to cycling and public transport earlier.  Let’s suppose that 20% of scooter rides are done instead of car ride.

In cities where we operate we have different amount of scooters per citizen. In heavily supplied cities like Nordic capitals can have up to a scooter per every 50-100 citizen. We can assume as a good starting point to have a scooter per every 200-300 citizen in London. This will give us around 30K scooters (all scooter players) with a possibility to grow to somewhat 50K scooters in city if it is proven to be a successful story.

With an average scooter utilisation of 5 rides / day, and given that 20% of rides in European cities are made instead of car ride, we can assume that we will save 30K*5*20%*365 = 30K car rides per day.

Even a single player, like Bolt, with 10K scooters fleet can contribute by saving 10K car rides per day.

In general, roughly 6.5M car/taxi/motorcycle trips made daily in London \[[http://content.tfl.gov.uk/travel-in-london-report-11.pdf|http://content.tfl.gov.uk/travel-in-london-report-11.pdf] (page 25)]

This means that all players can decrease a number of rides by roughly 0.5% (0.17% as an input of one player like Bolt) with a possibility to grow to somewhat 1%. This is not a game-changer if we speak about congestion though…

Hi Hannah and all

Just to clarify, there is absolutely no legal risk or employment grey area in having students work for us in Croatia, in the conditions of this 3-party agreement mentioned below (which is not something we can create, it's mandated by the law how it needs to be redacted, all we have to do is as the Employer fill in some details on the template provided by local authority). This is the email from the Croatian lawyers.

Dear Ioana,

 

In answer to your e-mail – yes, Ivan and Tomislav are basically correct. Student work is organized in Croatia in a special way and is regulated by the Act on performing student jobs. There is actually no classical employment and the student is not actually employed by anyone, rather,  their work is performed in a special way as regulated under the Act.

 

It is also correct that students can be engaged only via the intermediary  - the respective Student Centre, which is licensed by the Ministry of education. Pursuant the Act, an agreement is concluded between the Client (Bolt), the intermediary (Student center) and the Student.  Under the Agreement, the student undertakes to perform a certain job, the Client undertakes to pay a fee for the work performed, fees to the intermediary and contributions according to special regulations (all is paid to the Student Centre), while the student Centre undertakes to perform the activity of mediation and pay the remitted funds to the account of the Student.

 

You can not really influence the content of the above mentioned three party contract, since the contracts are signed on forms which are prescribed by the Ministry of education (the Contract mostly repeats the provisions of the Act) . Plus, General Terms and Conditions of the respective student center apply which are supplied with the contract, and should be considered as well.

 

Contracts are signed prior to the commencement of Student’s work, for a duration of at most 1 month (exceptionally 45 days with an explanation) and can be repeated (limits are prescribed by the Act), so Bolt will be, in general, in charge of the situation, and will not be bound long term with any of the students.  At the end of agreed period, Bolt shall specify the performed work hours and is obliged to pay the owed amounts in 15 days.

 

As for your question „Do we need an agreement that regulates who is responsible for the actions of the students whilst working for us? Otherwise, what do we do if they steal? If the leak dana?“, please be advised as follows.

 

It is prescribed by the Act that the Student is obliged to perform the work according to the instructions given by the client, in accordance with nature and type of work and  personally. Therefore, the student will be personally responsible to Bolt for the work performed. Of course, in practice, Bolt will not have too much of a recourse against the student, other than a law suit for (potential) damages and not hiring them the next month, but it is not much different with regular employees with whom the employee does not even have the same flexibility of canceling the agreement. There is practically no recourse against the Student center, since they offer the intermediary services and take no responsibility for the work performed.

 

Apart from the prescribed three party agreement, you can sign an additional agreement directly with the Student, specifying their obligation of confidentiality or some other obligations if applicable, for which they would take on a personal obligation towards Bolt (no effect to the obligations of the student Centre).

 

Just as a note, Bolt is obliged to provide the student with conditions for work in a safe manner and in a manner that does not endanger the health of the student, in accordance with the regulations governing safety at work and other regulations (i.e. same as for employees), and provide protection of dignity same as for employees (they also need to be able to contact the person appointed for dignity). Also, Bolt will have to keep a prescribed records with prescribed data on students as per the respective Bylaw  (Article 4 of the Bly law on employee records which regulated data on students). Although Labor act does not apply, students have certain rights e.g. 30 minute break if working more than 6 hours a day, increased salary in certain situations, etc.

 

Best regards,

 

Paula

Let’s say that there are two main factors why in reality this number could be lower:

* weather is not always good enough to ride a scooter
* despite we aim to, scooters are not always available for users. However, we apply a great effort to balance fleet within city. In Stockholm, for example, in 80% of cases users find a scooter within 100m.

So, let’s say 20% of short (up to 5km) car rides could be replaced with scooters.
Then we can save up to 2.8M ride-hailing rides per year, which is 2.63M kg of CO2 emissions.But this is a case how we can shift users from ride-hailing to scooters just by having both of them in one app. People are not only using ride-hailing, but also personal cars. Let’s look at a wider perspective.‘Micromobility and active travel in the UK’ research highlights that 36% of scooter rides worldwide are done instead of car rides. This value is lower in European cities, with 10-20% on average, as they are already seen a significant shift from private cars to cycling and public transport earlier. Let’s suppose that 20% of scooter rides are done instead of car [ride.In|http://ride.In] cities where we operate we have different amount of scooters per citizen. In heavily supplied cities like Nordic capitals can have up to a scooter per every 50-100 citizen. We can assume as a good starting point to have a scooter per every 200-300 citizen in London. This will give us around 30K scooters (all scooter players) with a possibility to grow to somewhat 50K scooters in city if it is proven to be a successful story.
With an average scooter utilisation of 5 rides / day, and given that 20% of scooter rides in European cities are made instead of car ride, we can assume that we will save 30K*5*20% = 30K car rides per day.
This will give an amazing 10.3M kg of CO2 emissions
Even a single player, like Bolt, with 10K scooters fleet can contribute by saving 10K car rides per [day.In|http://day.In] general, roughly 6.5M car/taxi/motorcycle trips made daily in London \[[http://content.tfl.gov.uk/travel-in-london-report-11.pdf|http://content.tfl.gov.uk/travel-in-london-report-11.pdf] (page 25)]

But answering your questions here 

* Do fleet drivers need a fleet owner’s approval to delete their account (driver’s account) on our platform?  In general, they don’t. * Can fleet owners request their fleet drivers’ details being changed (phone number, email, etc.)? It depends also on the relationship of the fleet and driver. Until we have this agreement, we should only make changes to driver’s data with request directly from the driver or with a written approval from driver sent by the fleet.
* Do fleet driver need a fleet owner’s approval to change driver’s personal data on the platform? In general, every person should have the right to change his/her personal information but again this is something that may be limited with contractual arrangements.

Hi Terver, 

The form of legal relationship here should be a binding service agreement and not MOU. The latter is not binding for the parties and express only an intention to act in a certain way without commitments.

The content of the service, place, time and manner of fulfilment of party’s obligations should be determined in the agreement. For example, donuts must be provided to Bolt for what time? Delivered where? The process of distributing the donuts to passengers, etc. How many social media posts will Bolt do? When? Within what timeframe? The content of the press release, social media posts, the value etc. Any risks or concerns you have with this cooperation? When all commercial terms and conditions are in place we can help preparing the service agreement.

# Sorry for misleading you with the first statement of the script. I should’ve had it removed from the *_alters.sql_* file. So the answer is *NO*, no change to the collation. Also, the {{general_ci}} is something that got automatically generated, I wasn’t aware what the correct value should be.
# Is this something that is absolutely required from our standards ? Because, I deliberately left it un-defaulted such that we’ll get an error if the code won’t provide any value at all. As opposed with having a default value where it could potentially hide a bug and corrupt the data, if the code by mistake left the value unset. The exact value of that column is contextual and important, that’s why I *would not* default to any value. Is this okay ?

About question no 2. this is a good example of misleading. 

Many developers are expecting without a default value, MySQL will give you an error but it won’t.

If you don’t provide any value to the column, it will choose the first enum value and insert.

So it will end up working exactly like below:



{noformat}`type` enum('pickup','segment','dropoff') NOT NULL,{noformat}

equals

{noformat}`type` enum('pickup','segment','dropoff') DEFAULT 'pickup' NOT NULL,{noformat}

lag(type,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by created asc) prev_type,
lag(value,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by created asc) prev_value,
lag(external_type,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by created asc) prev_external_type,
lag(external_id,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by created asc) prev_external_id,
datediff('second', lag(created,1) over (partition by vehicle_id order by created asc), created) diff_sec
from 
(	
select created, vehicle_id, type, value, charge, external_type, external_id, lat, lng
from rental.rental_order_vehicle_state_event
where created>date'2020-10-01'
and type = 'is_available_for_order' and value=0

Hello Ioana,



I am pleased to answer your questions regarding labour law of Czech Republic. If there will be any uncertainties, feel free to contact me.



Please be informed that I needed to clarify some factual aspects of your cooperation with people providing customer service. So firstly I had an in-depth conversation regarding the matter of possibilities of “semi-outsourcing” approaches in Bolt CZ with Roman Sysel and Michaela Pettersson. After I was informed of the nature of Bolt CZ needs, I can provide you with following brief analysis:



Your understanding of risk of re-qualification of service providers as employees if they fill the criteria of employees is absolutely correct. This is common problem also in landscape of Czech labour law, mainly because of tax and labour law implications of this distinction between employees and independent service providers. It is always more advantageous for employers to use independent service providers than regular employees – it is cheaper because of taxes regulation and it is favourable because the law does not protect independent providers nearly as much as employees. This is the reason why Czech labour law strictly prohibits to use independent service providers as a cover up of factual employment of these persons. This means that if the nature of cooperation between employer and natural person meets criteria of employment, it is prohibited to cooperate with these persons as self-employed individuals and employer must hire them as its employees.



Czech courts have concluded general criteria that must be assessed to determine whether the independent provider meets criteria of employment as follows. If these criteria are mostly (not necessarily cumulatively) met, there is huge possibility that independent service provider is actually cover-up for factual employee:



* personal dependence of the provider on the employer;

* instructions of employer are binding on the provider;

* provider is integrated into the employer's organizational structure;

* the employer exercises control and disciplinary authority over the provider;

* the provider performs work on behalf of the employer;

* the provider performs work using the employer's resources;

* the stability of cooperation between provider and employer.



I understand that your goal is to have a workers (employees or independent providers) in the field of customer services with limited benefits, lower wage, fixed-term employment etc. From my legal perspective, this situation can be solved as follows:



* You can hire new employees as “second grade” customer service for your current Bolt CZ legal entity. This group of new employees will deal with easier tasks and therefore will have a limited access to benefits, lower wage etc. Legally speaking this is completely viable option, because labour law does not impose an obligation to treat all your employees equally as long as different groups of employees are doing different job (there is only an obligation to ensure equal treatment in comparable jobs).

* You can hire self-employed independent customer service providers for your current Bolt CZ legal entity. This option is risky because these providers can qualify as employees if your cooperation with these providers meets abovementioned criteria. Danger of this legal outcome is even bigger because you will use two groups of workers (employers and independent providers) doing basically the same job under very similar circumstances.

* You can create new legal entity and hire new employees as “second grade” customer service by this new entity. This approach is very similar to first option. The advantage of this approach is that it will not be necessary to explain to employees why employees of one employer have different conditions of employment. There will be two employers: “first grade” customer service employees will be employed by Bolt CZ and “second grade” employees will be employed by new legal entity and therefore it is obvious that each employer treats its employees independently.

* You can create new legal entity and hire self-employed independent customer service providers by this entity. This is safer version of option 2, nevertheless the new entity must carefully consider whether the abovementioned criteria are met or not.

* You can use services of the personnel leasing company (as you mentioned). This is similar as using the outsource partner. Main difference is that employees of the personnel leasing company are allocated to Bolt CZ as user of their services. Bolt CZ will give them instructions and exercise the control over them. Bolt CZ must ensure that employees of personnel leasing company are treated equally as its own employees. Employees of personnel leasing company are paid by the leasing company and Bolt CZ must pay the fee to personnel leasing company.

* You can use the outsource partner.



As I wrote before – for you as an employer it is always better and easier to handle to use the services of independent providers (it is more flexible, because there is less restrictions than in the case of employees). On the other hand while you are using these providers you must consider the nature of cooperation with these subjects and set the rules of cooperation accordingly in order to avoid negative legal circumstances. Simply said – you must ensure that independent providers are truly independent.



When me and Michaela Pettersson discussed the possible general terms of your independent providers we both preliminarily agreed that abovementioned criteria are mostly met, which means that it is not legal to cooperate with these workers as independent providers in the field of customer service. Nevertheless this does not mean that it is impossible to create the model of cooperation with independent customer service providers, which suits your needs and does not qualify them as employees. The Czech courts have recently assessed these cases relatively benevolently – borderline cases are usually decided in favour of contractual freedom than (over)protecting factual employees. Therefore, if there is uncertainty as to whether the provider is truly independent, the courts tend to decide on independence.



If you opt for the variant of hiring self-employed independent providers, I suggest to discuss this matter with me as I can provide you my legal assessment of degree of planned independence of providers or help you to raise this degree of independence.



I hope that I fully answered your questions and I am ready to discuss this matter even further.



Have a nice weekend,

The proposed refund policies (agreed with the French OPS team):

* A user can’t find the reserved scooter/e-bike: first agents check the location of the e-vehicle, then report to the local OPS team if it is parked incorrectly). The process - [User Can't Find Reserved Scooter or E-bike|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360008647574--User-Can-t-Find-Reserved-Scooter-or-E-bike]
* A scooter/e-bike malfunctioned: first agents ask for a photo to confirm the e-vehicle condition, then, if needed, report to the local OPS team). The process - [User Reports Scooter or E-bike Malfunctioned|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013565000--User-Reports-Scooter-or-E-bike-Malfunctioned]
* A user is charged a fine because of the GPS issue: first agents check the map in Admin. The process - [User Reports Getting a Fine|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360008729834--User-Reports-Getting-a-Fine]
* A user couldn’t end a trip because of any tech issues: agents ask for a screenshot or a video to confirm and then escalating to the technical support team if needed; if a sum of overcharge is small, we can propose a promo code for an RH ride, but the user has a right to reject it. The process - [User Unable to End Scooter or E-bike Trip|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013546240--User-Unable-to-End-Scooter-or-E-bike-Trip]
* A user has been involved in an accident. The process - [Scooter or E-bike User Reports an Accident|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013632140--Scooter-or-E-bike-User-Reports-an-Accident]

Thus, we do not recommend to refund rides when a user forgot to end a trip or was charged a fine correctly.

This is the advertorial’s full text:

*“With Voi announcing plans to deploy up to 10,000 scooters in Oslo next year, we have to talk about how many electric scooters the different companies have in the streets of Oslo.*

 

I work in an industry that probably does not need any further introduction. Electric scooters give users enormous flexibility in everyday life and are an important part of transforming our cities towards becoming more sustainable. But the transition to this completely new form of passenger transport has led to some childhood diseases. This has made the scooters loved by some, and hated by others. I will not speculate on the relationship between the two, but I will keep saying what everyone - my colleagues included - thinks: something must be done. The situation requires a solution, and we and our competitors work closely with the City of Oslo to find these.

 

This year's debate, on the other hand, lacked an important nuance, namely the concrete measures that the various companies have taken to improve the situation. At the moment, there is a race for the authorities' favor. Collaborations are launched with non-profit organizations, own parking lots, free travel for essential workers, and many other positive contributions to society. Many of these measures are good, but they do not solve the most concrete problem the city faces*. With one operator recently disclosing ambitions to bring almost 10,000 scooters to the city, we believe the issue has to be addressed, and quickly:* there are too many scooters in the streets of Oslo\!

 

Yes, *it could be argued that* we at Bolt have contributed to the problem of our presence. At the same time, *we believe that every city has capacity for a certain number of scooters. To ensure electric scooters remain beneficial, this number has to be respected. We’re constantly deferring to various external factors - like a city’s size, topography, existing infrastructure - to make sure our electric scooters are solving problems, not causing them.* *As a result,* we were one of the players with the lowest number of electric scooters when we had launched the entire fleet, and since then we have even reduced our fleet further in Oslo, when we moved a share of it to Lillestrøm and Fredrikstad in connection with the launches there. In other words, we entered the Norwegian market with the aim of showing our citizens and competitors that it is possible to operate with a reasonable fleet size at a competitive price, with high utilization.

 

We believe that the right focus for a micro-mobility company is not to have the highest possible number of electric scooters, but rather to find out how we ensure the best utilization and availability of a sustainable and responsible amount. We at Bolt do this by having our own patrol that works to re-park and re-balance incorrectly parked electric scooters, place them evenly throughout the city, and ensure that they are in good condition.

 

But responsibility is about more than just fleet size. It is also about user safety. To reduce the risk of injury in potential accidents, we were the first player in Oslo to slow down at night in specific areas during the weekends. In addition, we have a separate Safety Toolkit in the app, which gives users clear instructions on how to park correctly and how to drive in a safe manner. We also know that many of the accidents happen because users are not used to riding electric scooters. That's why we have our own Beginner's Mode, which reduces both top speed and acceleration.

 

As of today, Bolt has fre*under 1000* electric scooters in Oslo, distributed both in the city center and various districts. *At the time of writing, this number is the appropriate amount that strikes a healthy balance for the existing supply and demand. Alas,* this is well below half of what we estimate that both of the two large established companies have separately. *One operator has even disclosed plans to bring close to 10,000 scooters to the city.* It's nice to see that they are now taking action by hiring people who are dedicated to fixing incorrectly parked scooters (we at Bolt have already had this for a long time, because we knew it would be necessary), but in the name of honesty - this alone does not solve the problem.

 

There are many indications that it is moving in a direction where there will be no room for an unlimited number of actors, the current situation has shown us that a total release does not work. At the same time, we believe it is very important that there is room for more than one player. We need a regulation where we ensure healthy competition, without it being at the expense of the product and user experience.

 

We know that it takes time to design such a regulation, and while we wait for it, I hope that my industry colleagues and competitors get together and contribute where it actually matters: by reducing the number of electric scooters they offer to a reasonable level. If not, they will continue to ruin the situation for those who need the service the most - the customers and the city.”

Loodan, et teie tervislik seisund on vahepeal paranenud ja tunnete end paremini kui varasemalt. Ühtlasi vabandan, et vastus teie eelmisele kirjale on mõnevõrra viibinud - tegelesime õigusosakonnas olukorra kaardistamisega. 


Nagu kolleeg Martin teile kirjutas, on meil teie nõudega edasi minemiseks vaja esmalt ülevaadet selle kohta, millistest elementidest teie poolt esitatud kahjunõue koosneb – st milline summa väljendab mittevaralist kahju, milline summa saamata jäänud töötasu ning milline summa jooksvaid kulusid ravimitele, abivahenditele, arsti visiitidele jne.


Jooksvate kulude tõendamiseks sobib igasugune tõend, mis näitab, millal ja mille eest konkreetne kulutus tehti. On täiesti arusaadav, et kõiki kuludokumente/ostutšekke ei pruugi alles olla, kuid enamik juhtudel peaks olema võimalik küsida tšekkide varukoopiaid, sest tänapäeval on enamik kassasüsteeme digitaalsed. Juhul, kui see ei peaks võimalik olema, palun edastage meile maksekorralduse väljavõtted koos kirjeldusega, mida osteti.


Saamata jäänud töötasu osas palume, et esitaksite meile tõendi selle kohta, kui kaua te olite haiguslehel ja milline on teie ühe päeva töötasu. Haiguslehe koopia peaks saama kas raamatupidajalt või perearstilt. Töötasu tõendina võite esitada ka enda töölepingu, sest saame selle edastada anonüümsel kujul meie raamatupidajatele ja paluda neil välja arvutada selle summa, mida pole tööandja ja haigekassa teile seaduse alusel hüvitanud (esimesed haiguspäevad).


Samuti oleks meil vaja arstitõendit, mis kinnitaks sõrmeluu mõra ning pea-ja rindkere põrutust.


Kui ülalkirjeldatud andmed on koos, saan teile anda tagasiside selle kohta, millise summa me saame teile kompenseerida.


Mõistame, et nende andmete kokkukogumine võtab aega, kuid kahjuks on need andmed vajalikud, sest igal väljamaksel peab olema alus.

In this file it’s possible to play with variables (yellow).I’ve prepared calculations for different OPS cycle cost (2.5 - 5 Eur) and two variants of estimations:
*Variant 1* - with higher battery capacity we need less charging -> cycle length increases, we save OPS costs per ride, as we do them less frequently. We do not capture lost because of discharged scooter rides.



*Variant 2* - with higher battery capacity and the same cycle length we get more rides (rides that were lost because of uncharge scooters). 9.3% extra charge means that we can get *only first* lost ride from scooter. Say, scooter was discharged and scanned 5 times, with higher battery capacity we can turn first failed scan into ride, but 4 others will remain failed. We will not save costs on OPS, as frequency of OPS will remain the same.
Also need to remember that 40% of failed scans actually do convert into ride, but on another scooter.



*Result*

* It’s easier to payback VÄLK with extended battery, than COBRA, as less frequent charges bring more impact in case of non-swappable batteries, because they are more expensive.
* The higher the OPS costs per cycle  - the easier to payback 20 extra Euros. So this makes more sense on high-costs markets
* Crucial parameter here is scooter lifetime. Obviously, the higher it is, the easier to payback. More interesting here is to check how easier. I’d say that it’s reasonable to assume that lifetime is between 1000 and 3000 rides.
* Picture below shows the *period of payback (in rides)* of additional 20 Euros, depending on OPS cost and scooter lifetime.
* If lifetime of scooter is less than 1500 rides, then we shouldn’t invest in extended batteries for both models. With lifetime between 1500 and 2000 we can try for VÄLK
* With lifetime +2K rides, we will payback these 20 Eur/scooter,  payback period will be between 1/2 year and year

Between two “strategies”: collect less often or capture lost rides - we can select one or another:


* on markets with high OPS costs better to collect less frequently
* on markets with low OPS costs better to try capturing lost rides

Hi Michaela

Please find below the answers to your Qs, I checked these by Matej so if you need further details let me know:

* *Can we hire for a fixed term?* 

YES. A fixed-term employment relationship between the same contracting parties (same employer and same employee) may not exceed 3 years (as of the date of the first fixed-term employment relationship) and it may be recurrently agreed *no more than twice*. An extension of an employment relationship shall also be considered as a recurrently agreed employment relationship.

And

Where an employer agrees with an employee the duration of an employment relationship for a fixed term contrary to previous subsection and where the employee notifies in writing the employer before the expiry of the agreed fixed term that he insists on being further employed (by this employer), *it shall apply that it is an employment relationship for an indefinite period.*

* *How long would it take to draft contracts for fixed term employees?* 

Same as a standard contract, we have templates ready. would need a few days notice of course 🙂 

* *What is the shortest period we can hire people for? 3 months? 4? 6?*

Employer’s decision, you can hire fixed term employees even for one day. However, be aware that in the sense of the above mentioned you can extend the employment relationship only twice (always by a maximum of 3 years).

* *What is the probation and notice period in these cases?*

*Probation periods*

The probation period may not be longer than *one half of the agreed period of the employment relationship.*

And

 A trial period may not be longer than three consecutive months from the date when the employment relationship commences, or six consecutive months from the date of commencement of the employment relationship where it concerns a managerial employee.

 And

 An agreed trial period may not be subsequently extended.

*Notice periods*
Notice of Termination given by the Employer/Employee:

The notice period must be the same for both the employer and the employee and shall be *at least two months*. The notice period is *always the same regardless of the length of the fixed term contract*. However, the employment relationship always ends no later than the last day of fixed term.

The notice period shall start to run on the first day of the calendar month following delivery (service) of the notice and come to an end upon the expiry of the last day of the relevant calendar month (there are exceptions for specific cases provided by law).

 Immediate Termination of an Employment Relationship given by the Employer/Employee:

There is no notice period and the employment relationship is terminated immediately upon receiving the respective letter (this legal institute of termination of Employment Relationship is usable only in cases of the most serious breaches of obligations).

* *Can these people have lower salary than our indefinite term in-house employees?*

If your fixed term employees are doing the same/similar role as indefinite term employees you must treat them equally including the equal salary. Czech Labour Law emphasizes the obligation to ensure equal treatment in comparable jobs. 

* *Can we not grant them any benefits?*

Employers shall ensure equal treatment for all employees as regards employee working conditions, remuneration for work and other elements in cash and in kind (of monetary value - such as benefits). Any form of discrimination in labour relations is prohibited.

Discrimination is defined as conduct in which one person is treated less favourably than another in a comparable situation, which is prohibited by law.

There is no discrimination or unequal treatment in cases where benefits are provided on the basis of a factual reason consisting in the nature of the work or activity performed and the requirements applied are proportionate to this nature. Therefore, it is not unequal treatment if the reasons for providing benefits are, for example, qualifications, length of experience or number of years of service, job position, work results and their results for employers, etc.

however, if you provide benefits to your indefinite term employees without any specific conditions, you should also provide these same benefits to fixed term employees in the same/similar position. Only if benefits were set up from the start with rules around granting them, which currently they are not, could you be allowed not to offer fixed term people the same benefits.

*_So in short answer, in the current benefit set up we have at a global level, we have to grant them the same benefits as indefinite employees._*

a demo on how successive fixed term contract rules work:

Between Bolt and the same employee, you can only conclude a maximum fixed term agreements as follows:

Contract A – initial one

Contract B – first extension

Contract C – second extension

Contract C is the last (and second) fixed term extension you can offer. This means you are allowed to extend the fixed term contract once (Contract B) and then a second time (Contract C). After Contract C expires, you must employ that person for an indefinite time or they cannot work for you again on another fixed term.

I had a sync with Micah today and think there has been a bit of a misunderstanding here so I want to clarify. 

Micah expressed that it is not his desire to see fleet owners invoice us for the marketing services. He would like to see that these payments are made to drivers. Further, his understanding is that these payments are conditional on *activity*-related requirements. 

*Issue*: If we are paying a fleet for this service through invoices and they do not employ the drivers they engage (those drivers just contract with them for use of car) then we have no right to regulate the drivers ‘working’ conditions through an agreement with the fleet. Drivers in those cases have an independent contract with Bolt to use the platform. We cannot claim some third party contract can be imposed onto them. 

*Solutions:* In order to enforce activity related marketing service, you have three options.

# Engage with fleets who are bringing drivers onto the Bolt platform as their employees. Then we have a right to request certain activity as part of the services when paying this fleet. However, I understand from Micah this is not feasible in TZ
# Contract with fleets directly for payment in relation to marketing service in a way that does not impact drivers in their use of the platform. This would require creative thinking from ops on what instead to regulate (number of cars, number of weeks branded before payment etc) 
# Contract any pay drivers (like the KE model) for the marketing services where we then have a right to agree with them basic activity levels. Micah has expressed that the issue here is that drivers dont own the cars and therefore can do this without the owners permission which creates issues. {code:sql}select *,
1.0*scooter_orders/(scooter_orders+finished_orders_rh),
1.0*(gmv_rh+gmv_scooters)/search_users_rh
from
(select 
	treatment_id,
	search_categories_overview__city_id city_id,
	count(distinct search_categories_overview__session_id) as search_sessions_rh, 
	count(distinct search_categories_overview__user_id) as search_users_rh,
	count(distinct case when company_order__state='finished' then company_order__id else null end) as finished_orders_rh,
	sum(case when company_order__state='finished' then company_order_try__ride_price/cer.rate else null end) as gmv_rh,
	1.0*finished_orders_rh/search_sessions_rh rh_session_to_finished_order,
	avg(company_order_try__ride_distance) avg_rh_dist
FROM public.etl_search_denormalized_view sd
join targeting_enrollment e on sd.search_categories_overview__user_id=e.auth_id
join vw_currency_exchange_rates AS cer
   ON sd.company_order_try__price_currency = cer.currency
   AND trunc(sd.company_order__created) = trunc(cer.valid_on)
where search_categories_overview__created>date'2020-10-13' and search_categories_overview__created<date'2020-10-21'
and e.treatment_id in (3522,3523)
group by 1,2
order by 2 asc, 1 asc) rh
left join 
(
select 
	treatment_id,
	o.city_id,
	count(distinct o.id) as scooter_orders,
	sum(price/cer.rate) as gmv_scooters
FROM rental.rental_order_order o
join targeting_enrollment e on o.user_id=e.auth_id
join vw_currency_exchange_rates AS cer
   ON o.currency = cer.currency
   AND trunc(o.created) = trunc(cer.valid_on)
where o.created>date'2020-10-13' and o.created<date'2020-10-21'
and e.treatment_id in (3522,3523)
group by 1,2
order by 2 asc, 1 asc
) sc
on rh.treatment_id=sc.treatment_id and rh.city_id=sc.city_id
{code}

Hey Inga\! Interesting idea. 

However from the legal perspective, I do not think we can claim ‘fair-use’ here. 

We have to remember that song lyrics are the intellectual property of the author. Therefore, we cannot use them in our advertising (which by nature is to our profit) without permission *except* where the author's rights are no longer valid (generally only the case 70+ years after death of the author). 

Using these without permission comes with the risk of (in the best case) cease and desist, (in the worst-case) IP infringement claim and damages. Of course, EOD it is a business decision. However, our advice would be that we obtain written permission in the form of an agreement prior to use.

If you are interested in knowing more about “fair-use” I think this article summarizes quite well: [https://fairuse.stanford.edu/overview/fair-use/what-is-fair-use/#:~:text=In its most general sense,permission from the copyright owner.|https://fairuse.stanford.edu/overview/fair-use/what-is-fair-use/#:~:text=In%20its%20most%20general%20sense,permission%20from%20the%20copyright%20owner.]

Even though that we decided at the beginning of 2020 that annual leaves can be taken as working days then according to the law it still works in calendar days, meaning that these “extra” days that you can see on your payslip are the weekend days (you applied for 15 days of leave, but in addition to that there are 4 weekend days included, so 19 days all together).

In October there’s 31 days but in November 30 days (for an example, monthly pay is 1000€, then in Oct day pay would be 1000/31= 32.26 but for Nov the day pay would be 1000/30=33.3).

*TL;DR?* Please continue to escalate any such requests to legal and DPO, Greta. I will work on compliance this side to ensure we have a lawful basis in GDPR, and other obligations are met moving forward.

Full advice and DPO future actions:

Article 6(1)(c) of GDPR – legal obligation – establishes a GDPR lawful basis where a controller has to process personal data for “compliance with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject to.” This provision can only be relied upon where the legal obligation is laid down in EU or a Member State law *to which the controller is subject*. I would argue that a Lithuanian national law likely does not represent a legal obligation to which the controller, Bolt, is subject - a company established in Estonia.  The caveat to this is we’re still to map the Controllership model (say the request is received by, e.g., a Lithuanian subsidiary??) etc.

Bolt, I’d suggest, needs instead to disclose on a voluntary basis in response to valid legal process issued by EU member states on the basis of legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(f) GDPR). How do we do this? We’d call it a “good faith” belief - and protect the company this way.

In Facebook we had wording in the [+Privacy Notice+|https://www.facebook.com/policy.php] which read:

 “_How do we respond to legal requests or prevent harm?_

_In response to a legal request, if we have a good-faith belief that the law requires us to do so. We can also respond to legal requests when we have_ *_a good-faith belief that the response is required by law in that jurisdiction, affects users in that jurisdiction and is consistent with internationally recognised standards._*”

That expectation has not been set here with Drivers, I feel; I’m not satisfied that the Bolt Privacy Notice for Drivers covers, for one, the processing of this data, nor, second, the sharing of such data for the Lithuanian purposes above. 

Please continue to escalate any such requests to legal and DPO, Greta. I have not addressed the changing of bank details here. 

I will take an action to discuss with Silja the need for a policy position and establishing a standardized legal basis in GDPR for such requests - even then it will remain case-by-case. I’d also like to suggest to Legal a revision to the Bolt Privacy Notice for Drivers. The risk otherwise is a complaint escalation to the AKI with “scope creep” enquiries into broader Bolt data sharing practices with third parties.
