DEMO OF GH-OST ALTER TABLE ON SHARDED AND UNSHARDED KEYSPACES

This is a simple Proof of Concept to evaluate Vitess and gh-ost integration for online schema changes. Documentation for this can be found [here|https://vitess.io/docs/user-guides/schema-changes/managed-online-schema-changes/#using-gh-ost].

The Vitess local [demo|https://vitess.io/docs/get-started/local/] example is used, high level steps are:

# Install prereqs, etcd, Vitess components
# Deploy a single unsharded keyspace named *commerce*
# Run _MoveTables_ process, goal is going from a single monolithic keyspace (*commerce*) to having multiple keyspaces (*commerce* and *customer*). 
# It involves creating the needed additional target tablets, creating shadow tables on new *customer* keyspace (MoveTables) and doing the cut-over when ready to switch (SwitchReads and SwitchWrites). Cleanup of original tables is done with _ DropSources_
# Resharding *customer/0* into two shards involves creating the additional tablets, preparing sequence tables, vschema and vindexes and issuing the _ Reshard_ command. Switching from single shard *customer/0* to *customer/\-80 customer/80\-* is done via SwitchReads and SwitchWrites like previously.
# Finally the old customer/0 tablets are destroyed and topology updated with DeleteShard
# Alter table on unsharded table
# Alter table on sharded table 
# {color:red} TODO: verify that old gh-ost shadow tables get cleaned up {color} => So far I've been manually deleting gh-ost tables directly on mysqlds (bypassing vtgate). This is not ideal => need to investigate Vitess table lifecycle management [here|https://vitess.io/docs/reference/features/table-lifecycle/] and [here|https://vitess.io/docs/user-guides/schema-changes/managed-online-schema-changes/#table-cleanup] => *UPDATE: tested with Vitess 9.0 and now table lifecycle works out of the box.*

SHOW Statements
Vitess supports a few additional options with the SHOW statement.

SHOW keyspaces – A list of keyspaces available.
SHOW vitess_tablets – Information about the current Vitess tablets such as the keyspace, key ranges, tablet type, hostname, and status.
SHOW vitess_shards – A list of shards that are available.
SHOW vschema tables – A list of tables available in the current keyspace’s vschema.
SHOW vschema vindexes – Information about the current keyspace’s vindexes such as the keyspace, name, type, params, and owner. Optionally supports an “ON” clause with a table name.

** _or 700_000 / (3600*_16) = ~12cases/sec (if instead of 24h we use 16h excluding sleep time)
** 8cases/sec = 8-16 rps /getVehicles we can save
** or if 12cases/sec = 12-24 rps we can save
* [Current RPS|http://nodemonitor.internal/graph/d/nIwkIOGWk/incoming-requests%5D%5BRPS%5D%5D]
** max 455

* Hence, we can save

_The risk of delivering/failing the delivery of the notice is carried by the lessee (as the sender in this case) under Belarusian legislation as well. _Moreover, failing the delivery of the notice within the term, specified in the lease agreement does not exclude the possibility of the parties to terminate the lease by not renewing it in case of the parties agreement and proper performance of the premises return procedure._

Hi all,

*Problem:*

Fleet partner in UA requests us to transfer funds (the fare for rides taken minus Bolt's commission + different regular bonuses we provide) to third person non-UA bank account to avoid UA taxes.

*For context:* 

Commerce has requested legal clearance before remitting any further funds. However, any further delay in transfers likely results in serious negative impact to our supply as the respective fleet is a key partner.

*Questions:* 

# Do we have proper legal basis for transferring the funds?
# Does our involvement in allowing respective transfers provide Ukrainian Government or law enforcement agencies thereof with the grounds of bringing any charges against us in particular related to (1) going around currency control regime (2) tax evasion or (3) money laundering?

*Conclusion&suggestions*

Initial query shows no legal risks for Bolt. Some aspects need further investigation, but for the time being potential risk can be considered relatively low. +Suggest NOT to keep the payments pending from legal perspective.+


*Rationale:* 

*Legal basis for transfer*

* *Who is our contracting party for executing those payments?* 

It's the fleet partner who signs up to Bolt platform and accepts the T&C, and also signs up its individual drivers. 

* On what terms and how we contract?

The fleet partner has accepted the UA Driver T&C's [https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/legal/ua/terms-for-drivers/|https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/legal/ua/terms-for-drivers/] by ticking the relevant check box during sign-up. 

The practice differs by country, e.g in EE, KZ, AM we sign hard copies + have fleet drivers also accept T&C's directly during sign-up.

Point 2.1 of the UA Driver T&C elaborates on the conclusion of the contract, points 2.3, 2.4 on the role of the fleet in performing on behalf of the drivers,

point 2.2 on the bank transfer specifics, including the right and obligation for us to transfer to the bank account named by the fleet partner  p 6.1 provides Bolt the right to act as fleet partners payment agent,

Point 4.6 provides the fleet partner the right for the fare for the rides taken, p 5.2 specifies Bolt's right to commission fee, p 6 provides basis for minimum income bonuses.

According to my best understanding we are doing payouts to the fleet in several batches (that as such is no direct concern) without indicating which exact part of it is the fare, what part is bonus and which bonus. Still, I also don't consider this as a major issue as long as the sums add up. 

Another matter is that we have different bonuses, but only minimum income one's are clearly reflected in the contract.

Bringing more clarity to this going forward is also in Legal team's roadmap, but there is no quick fix, and its not urgent as the critical contractual language is in place.


Afaik another matter here is the question why is the particular third party collecting money on behalf of more than 10 "fleets". As I understand one has to distinguish here between "fleet as a legal entity do whom we contract", and "fleets indicated in our Admin system". I understand its due to our system specifics why we have "cut" one fleet down to several (one fleet has different fleet name/number for different cities in our system) and that causes the external image as if the money for several fleets was transferred to this one fleets account. But its not the case legally - legally its still one fleet partner. I see its for us to fix this internally, but its no reason to park any payouts.

* How is it tracked what are the terms agreed upon?

Log files from fleets sign-up need to be matched with the T&C web-page log files (considering possible later updates of the T&C) to detect the applicable T&C. 

It's a setup from pre-Legal team, and overall there is room for improvement, but this is how we currently do online contracting so it's no reason to park any payouts.



*Any legal provision we might violate by accepting such transfers?*

Memorandum provided by ePravo did not outline any risks from UA perspective, however as the argumentation and the key conclusion were poor we would request a second opinion from PwC UA. 

Nevertheless I see it as no reason to hold the payouts. Such analysis would result the same e.g in EE - there's no  direct legal risk for Bolt.

Also, I am not convinced if the UA laws are that relevant at all considering that the in-app money never crosses UA border, but is paid out via some Adyen(?) EU, and not UA, accounts

*Suggest to have a quick call instead of creating long thread if needed.*

Article 33 of the GDPR requires Bolt to notify the relevant data protection authorty no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach, *unless* the personal data breach is “*unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons*”. Article 34 requires Bolt to notify the affected data subjects *without delay* when a personal data breach is “*likely to result in a high risk* to the rights and freedoms of natural persons”.

In both Articles 33 and 34, a risk assessment needs to be completed in a timely manner. 

Bolt needs clear procedure and a risk assessment methodology for determining whether a personal data breach triggers the “high risk” threshold for notification. The assessment of risk needs to be conducted objectively.

Dear Taylor,

I hope this email finds you well.

Thanks for contacting Bolt on 07 September 2020. You submitted a request for the disclosure of your personal data under the right of subject access. Further correspondence followed with my colleague, namely, Kaija, including a partial refusal on 06 October 2020.

My name is Calum Liddle, and I have recently joined Bolt as the Data Protection Officer. You're likley aware that the DPO is mandated to provide advice to, on my part, Bolt, on its data protection obligations, including those under the General Data Protection Regulation. The DPO may also be contacted by data subjects, such as yourself, with regards to exercising rights, including the right of subject access.

I have reviewed the correspondence between you and Bolt to date with regards to your request for subject access - and I'm eager to bring about a resolution which upholds, of course, your right to your personal data as far as the GDPR intends.

To that extent I am keen, Taylor, to help further identify the information you, in actual fact, want to receive. No bundle has been prepared yet. But I am told by staff that, despite your short tenure, the bundle would be large and, in turn, the preparation of a disclosure excessive. If further clarification was provided, Bolt may be able to extract faster, and more precisely, the personal data really sought and avoid working through a large catch-all bundle which would be argued to be excessive. +*_So I ask, in line with the GDPR, whether you might specify the information or processing activities to which your request, in actual fact, relates?_*+

For example, might you be able to detail a substantive topic or theme to help refine a search in Slack and the email inbox? Refining the scope with, for example, a thematic search, will help reduce the excessiveness of the search and, in turn, the disclosure to be prepared. Bolt is otherwise relying on a feat of reading, extraction and, where appropriate, redaction of all that which has been caught by the current request. Urging such an effort to be made by Bolt, nonetheless, may not necessarily provide the disclosure sought. 

There are few exemptions to the right to subject access, Taylor: you've outlined these in your correspondence, and, indeed, excessiveness is one such exemption. But there are further limitations and nuances to the right, too. For one, the disclosure is limited to that which constitutes your personal data. The very nature of the request rests in those correspondence channels used between other employees, making the task, the Controller says, troublesome and resource intensive. This is understandable as, in line with the expectations of the GDPR, Bolt will have to undertake a task excluding or redacting on balance with other fundamental rights and freedoms, too: this includes protecting the rights and freedoms of others and their privacy, of course, and Bolt's freedom to undertake business activities which includes the protection of, for example, confidential activities related to Bolt's enterprise, too.

I hope you might be able to specify the information or processing activities to which your request relates. I'd be happy to discuss this matter with you. My number is below.

You have the right, of course, to instead approach the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate or a court in order to appeal the earlier decision.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Best wishes,



Calum Liddle

Bolt has already confirmed the account was suspended on suspicion of fraudulent activity. The account has since been reinstated upon human review. \[Is this correct?]

The account was not suspended by soley automated means; we have human review systems in place which are alerted to accounts at risk, or suspended due to suspected breaches of terms, conditions or policies, and for legal and regulatory purposes also, including fraudulent activity.

The "reason for account blocking" - or, rather, suspension - has, therefore, been disclosed to you. It follows this part of your request has been fulfilled.

Turning to the request for logic, Bolt refuses to disclose the logic used in suspending or blocking accounts more generally. It is well known that technology companies, including Bolt, and those that process financial data for example, use rules and logic to help determine whether a user's account is at risk, or in breach of policy, which might warrant suspension.

Processing activities are already made transparent by way of the user facing Privacy Policies made readily available. Bolt also publishes behavioural expectations of drivers and riders - these too are shared. \[Is this a fair statement?]

Disclosure of the logic would reveal information concerning Bolt's safety, welfare and fraud prevention mechanisms, their thresholds and, indeed, effectiveness to those so inclined to know. Releasing this information, even partially in response to individual data subject access requests, is a harm too great. For example, if further requests were to be submitted for various periods of time, it may allow a person with the inclination to do so, to infer Bolt suspension thresholds, and provides a key to bad actors who may be inclined to 'game the system' or, in other words, endeavour to gain immunity from their efforts to break the law, defraud or breach terms. Bolt's attempts to protect accounts, users and its wider business activities would be prejudiced. Bad actors may utilise pieces of precise information concerning logic, no matter how small, allowing a ‘bigger picture’ to be revealed and such a cumulative effect of disclosures will lead to even further prejudice.

On weighting of the rights and freedoms of others, including the increased risk to other users and their safety, account integrity, and Bolt's own commercial purposes in protecting its enterprise, Bolt moves to refuse such any further disclosure concerning logic.

I trust this explanation, while disappointing in achieving a disclosure, is helpful in at least providing the reassurance around Bolt's processing activities.

Bolt consulted its Data Protection Officer for the purposes of Art.39(1) and preparing this response to you.

Lastly, you mentioned your intention to approach the Latvian DPA. Our lead supervisory authority is the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate. Dear Ioana,

 

I am glad to answer your question as follows:

 

* It is not possible to unilaterally order your part time employees to work overtime. This means that part time employees must agree with overtime work. Employees may agree to work overtime in advance (I recommend to obtain their consent with overtime work in writing).

 

* Every hour of employee´s overtime work up to 40 hours per week is paid the same way as an hour of work during basic working hours.

 

Every hour of overtime work over 40 hours per week must be paid with an overtime bonus. Overtime bonus is basic salary plus at least 25% of average earnings per hour, unless the employer and the employee have not agreed to provide compensatory holiday to the extent of overtime work instead of overtime bonus.

 

Example: Your employee is contracted to work for 30 hours a week. His basic hour salary is 200 CZK per hour. This employee works:

 

a)            30 basic hours and 5 hours overtime per week – you must pay him basic salary (30 h. * 200 CZK) plus earnings per overtime work under 40 hours per week (5 h. * 200 CZK). He worked less than 40 hours per week in total, which means that he is not eligible for overtime salary bonus, therefore his hourly overtime salary is the same as basic salary.

 

b)           30 basic hours and 15 hours overtime per week – you must pay him basic salary (30 h. * 200 CZK) plus earnings per overtime work under 40 hours per week (10 h. * 200 CZK) plus earning per overtime work over 40 hours per week with 25% bonus (5 h. * 250 CZK) or 5 hours of compensatory holiday (if you agree with employee to choose this option).

 

If you need to clarify some other circumstances, feel free to contact me. I´m happy to help you.

 

Have a nice day,

 

*Matěj Krupa*

 

Janstová & Smetana

Attorneys at Law

Of course don’t forget that for some who does a full time role, or 40 hours per week, the rule of overtime in general applies which is:

An employee may not be ordered to do more than *8 hours* of overtime work within individual weeks and *150 hours* of overtime work within one calendar year. The employer may request overtime work beyond the scope set out in the previous sentence *only on the basis of agreement with the employee.*

So bottom line is, for any overtime work, always *get agreement from employee in writing* and try not to go beyond total working time of *48 hours within a working week*.

Dear Andy et All, 

# This is the wording you could use in the offer letter.

“_Please note that this offer is contingent you not having valid criminal punishments. This means we cannot enter into employment relationship with you before we receive an extract of your country of residence’s official criminal records database stating you have no valid criminal punishments_.”

2. I noticed that we already have a clause in the EC General Terms where the employee confirms he/she has provided accurate information (should be clause 9.7).  However, I adjusted the wording a bit, so please use the following wording. This wording can be used in all employment contracts.

“_By signing the Contract, the Employee confirms that he/she has provided to the Employer accurate and true information about his/her professional experience and skills, abilities, education and personal characteristics. The Employee confirms that he/she has no valid criminal punishments. The Employee confirms that there are no hindrances or conflict of interests that would prevent the Employee to perform his/her duties excellently in the interests of the Employer as of the moment of commencement of work_.”

 On a general note (and as discussed in the meeting), Estonian law does not specifically set forth any terms and conditions for background checks (pre-employment or otherwise). However, under Estonian employment law, the employer may ask the candidate or the employee only such information in which the employer has justified interest in and usually this means information related to the suitability of the employee for the position. This is combined with the purpose of limitation and minimality principles under GDPR. The absence of the employer’s legitimate interest is presumed first of all in the case of questions which disproportionately concern the private life of the person or which are not related to his/her suitability for the job offered. So the employer should be able to explain with regard to all information checked or verified during background checks that it has justified interest in such information. 

In case we use the wordings in the offer letter and employment contract as suggested above and in case of negative results of the background check when employment contract is already concluded, annulment of the employment contract is an option, however applicability of this option should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.

The employer has a possibility to annul the employment contract due to mistake or fraud, relying on the information or false information about the employee with regard to which the employer had a legitimate interest. Thus, if the results of background checks are unsatisfactory and the employer had a legitimate interest to know such information, but the employee did not reveal such information earlier or lied about it, the employer has a ground for an annulment of employment contract. The employer may annul the employment contract due to mistake or fraud within two weeks as of learning about the mistake or fraud.

Please let me know if you have any additional questions. 

Regards

Häli

The purpose of the Regional Lead role is to lead a large team of CS People in pursuit of our Customer Support Purpose and role model our expected leadership values and attributes. 




* Role model pursuit of our Customer Support purpose:
** Provide Customer experience feedback to the business so we can improve our products and services.
** Solve Customer issues and make it feel easy so Customers continue to use our products and services.
** Deliver high levels of Stakeholder engagement - giving us the credibility to influence the Customer experience
* Be a role model leading our support readiness for existing and predicted challenges and share ideas to decrease the workload and improve the quality & speed of Bolt’s customer support
* Contribute to your peers success through collaboration, creativity and giving critical constructive feedback.
* Identify problems and opportunities to support our purpose and then initiative, own and contribute to solutions. 
* Ensure your People are highly engaged: 
** Drive clarity of purpose to ensure your people understand their work matters
** Drive a diverse and inclusive environment to ensure all of your people know their opinions matter
** Drive empowerment to ensure all of your people know their decisions matter
** Drive Recognition to ensure all of your people know their contributions matter
** Drive Growth to ensure all of your people know their ambitions matter 
* Lead initiatives within and beyond Customer Support to drive down the size of incoming support volume.

h3. ....demonstrate our Leadership values and attributes:

* Drive – our Leaders are hard working, able to tackle large challenges with enthusiasm
* Intelligence – our Leaders are able to learn and solve new problems - they can troubleshoot logically, create scalable and repeatable processes
* Integrity – our Leaders are respectful, ethical and trustworthy
* Empathy - our Leaders can relate to our Customers and their colleagues, they seek to understand different views
* Coach-ability - our Leaders actively seek out, listen to and act on constructive feedback
* Team players - our Leaders collaborate openly and contribute to each others success
* Humility - our leaders don’t need to be the smartest in the room, or be right - they seek out the best decisions and solutions always putting Bolt, and the Team ahead of their own ego
* Growth mindset - our Leaders coach their teams for success, they understand learning from mistakes makes us better Leaders
* Our Leaders build teams with[ |https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LhoLuui9gX8]psychological safety
* Our Leaders create more great Leader
